title: AssetTag Studio
summary: A browser-native utility that turns CSV and Excel inventory into printable QR and Code 128 labels while keeping asset data on the user's device.

problem: Equipment inventories already live in spreadsheets, but producing consistent physical labels often means copying identifiers into separate tools, guessing print dimensions or sending inventory to remote services.
purpose: Create a focused, account-free utility for importing inventory, designing QR or barcode labels and exporting physically sized PDF sheets without uploading spreadsheet values.
keyFeatures: Import CSV, XLSX and legacy XLS, choose a worksheet and review identifier/header diagnostics.
Search, sort, select and remove records without turning the workspace into a spreadsheet editor.
Generate QR codes from raw fields or payload templates, or printable ASCII Code 128 barcodes.
Configure label fields, ordering, prefixes, typography, dimensions, padding and borders.
Arrange labels on A4, Letter, A5 or custom pages with millimeter/inch inputs, margins and gaps.
Export multi-page PDFs with progress and cancellation; preview only a bounded subset of labels.
Use light/dark themes and remembered preferences while imported row values stay in memory.
role: Product scoping and end-to-end delivery across the browser-local architecture, spreadsheet import, label editor, rendering/layout engine, PDF generation, verification, documentation and deployment.
technicalHighlights: Normalize CSV and Excel into a generic string-valued dataset, preserving leading zeroes and supporting arbitrary column names.
Parse in a module worker with cancellation, a deadline, input quotas and structural ZIP/CFB validation before opening Excel files.
Use millimeters as the canonical layout unit and share canvas rendering between preview and physically positioned PDF labels.
Validate QR module density, quiet zones, Code 128 character/width bounds and text fit before producing output.
Bound DOM previews and render caches, yield between export batches and release decoded PDF image channels promptly.
Keep runtime processing on the device, persist only permitted preferences and enforce static security headers.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Different spreadsheet formats, malformed workbooks and stale asynchronous imports could produce inconsistent or excessive parser work.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Use one normalization contract, worker lifecycle/generation guards, readable diagnostics and file/row/column/cell/archive bounds.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Preview appearance alone does not guarantee that PDF labels have the right dimensions or scannable codes.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Calculate layout in millimeters, share the label renderer, preserve code quiet zones and validate actual PDF page dimensions and QR decoding in browser tests. Physical printer/scanner calibration remains a separate hardware check.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Large PDF batches can retain decoded image memory and freeze the interface.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Embed PDF images promptly, bound caches/previews, yield between batches and offer cancellation. Repeated-label boundary exports are verified; large unique-label export performance remains device-dependent and unbenchmarked.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: The custom hostname inherited a zone-wide Cloudflare analytics injection despite the app having no telemetry code.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Add a hostname-scoped Disable RUM rule and rerun hosted network/privacy tests while leaving the main portfolio's analytics intact.

resultsImpact: Deployed an account-free static application at tagstudio.zachcodes.dev with no backend or inventory upload API.
Verified 100 unit tests, including 36 synthetic sample-pack checks; the production browser suite has 16 passing scenarios in local Edge, CI Chromium and hosted Edge verification.
Verified a complete 834-page PDF from 20,000 repeated labels with the standard A4 layout; this is not a benchmark for 20,000 unique labels.
Provided a 30-file synthetic test pack, production screenshots, a 9.6-second demo and an 11-page A4 sample PDF containing 245 invented assets.
Preserved the privacy boundary with request/storage checks, constrained input/rendering paths and verified live security headers.
lessonsLearned: A shared data and rendering contract reduces differences between imported formats, previews and exported output.
Import acceptance and renderability are different boundaries: a valid spreadsheet cell may still be too long or dense for a printable label.
Hosting defaults need verification too; analytics injection can originate outside application source.
Repeated-label stress tests benefit from caching and must not be presented as evidence for equally sized unique-label workloads.
A small structured editor and static deployment keep the product focused and maintainable; named templates, extra code formats and printer profiles can follow measured user needs.
